reviews.text: It's amazing to play this classic game on android, but the controls for battles are lacking. You don't have the level of control of the PC version, and it's more cumbersome to do anything but basic commands. A big battle would get out of hand. I recommend setting combat difficulty to easy and autoresolving most battles, and mainly enjoy the campaign management gameplay. I havent tried using a bluetooth keyboard and mouse, but if that would give you PC controls, that would be perfect.
reviews.stars: Rated 4 stars out of five stars

reviews.text: While I had been aware of the Total war games for sometime, this is my first actual experience with it and I highly recommend it for anyone who enjoys strategy games. It runs smoothly on my Pixel 2, the graphics are good, considering when it was released, and the gameplay itself is in depth and well done. The controls are a little difficult at times, particularly when trying to rotate your army on the battle screen, but for the most part it works well enough as a phone port. Worth the $10 price.
reviews.stars: Rated 5 stars out of five stars

reviews.text: I didn't grow up playing this game on PC or its franchise and I've never been to happy with typical war/strategy game on mobile devices. It seems like they mostly focus on base building and not really into war and strategy tactics. This game fixes that and has so many ins and outs that I learn something each time playing. minutes turn to hours, hours to days and now I've been playing the same campaign for MONTHS. Unbeatable experience. Controls are a tad wack but no other complaints. NEED MORE!

reviews.text: I like the game. Only thing I wish it had would be historic events that occur during the gameplay, other than that thoroughly enjoy the challenging and variation gameplay available. On top of it, if you are finding the game a little to to challenging you can create characters to plant in your forces to help you get that little edge you might need.

reviews.text: This game is great! Pricing is perfectly reasonable and one time. Only notes I would have is that I would love to have an allied victory option in online games. I enjoy team games with friends and we don't want to have to turn on each other at the end. Also an 8 to 10hr turn limit game would be a nice option, something between 24hrs and 30 seconds. Also Cymanti is not quite balanced. All in all still 5 stars. Definitely one of the best games on the app store. I recommend it all the time.

reviews.text: This is a legitimate 4x game, not just a good "mobile" 4x game. Basically 2d Endless Space but with tactical battles, or MOO2 if you're old enough. Like all 4x games, it's complicated if you're new to the genre, but I'd say it's more streamlined than most (in a good way). If you're not new, you might want to ratchet up the difficulty a notch for your first game. It's worth way more that a dollar; screw freemium. If you want a good mobile 4x, spend the damn dollar and support the devs.

reviews.text: The lack of any good instructions makes this game overwhelming. Edit: after a few times going back and starting a game you do get used to the game, but it really is alot to take in at once. I still don't understand alot of it, and it gets hard to keep up with everything when your empire grows to even a small size of 8 - 10 worlds. The game will grow on you after a while, if you get passed the intimidation of the complexity, that was actually the hard part. Edit: needs a undo move button for ships, too easy to get them into places you never wanted them.

reviews.text: This is by far one of my favorite games to play. My husband and I have it on PC and mobile, but we mostly play it on mobile since it's more convenient. I love that it's co-op so my husband and I can team up as different clans with unique features, it gives you multiple victory conditions to work towards if you like to focus on economy or military victory. Our games do crash frequently, most of the time we can reconnect but sometimes we have to restart. Been playing for 3 years and still love it!

reviews.text: This game is a very good one. There are not many updates so I pause a lot of playing it, but without updates this game is the same size as it was so it's good. I like the graphics they are very good and unique. The two planets are good too, but I wish there was a third one for example Tantros. The variety of turrets and units is good too. And multiplayer is fun too, I spend a lot of time on it. Unit AI is great too but not the best (base builder AI). Overall 5 stars seems the best choice.

reviews.text: Masterpiece. Great game for people who like building factory games. Combines the elements of Tower Defense and Strategic warfare. I also recommend sandbox when you want a more slow paced relaxing play. I like the campaigns and adding a workshop is great. Multi-player is okay. I like the art as its very simple yet nice to see, and the soundtrack fits well. A few things I'd like to see is more music, maybe a intense soundtrack and a calm one. I also would say the same for the art. Love it. ★★★★★!

reviews.text: A rare diamond of a game in the current market! This game is truly free and has no ads or micro-transactions, which is super rare for a game of this quality. It's obviously a passion project and very addictive, with tons of stuff to do and high replay value. I had never played the Civilization games, so it took me a little while to figure out what was going on here, but after you get the hang of it, then the game becomes very engrossing and fun. The graphics are simple but sufficient.

reviews.text: This is the best mobile game out there in my opinion. It's based off my favorite game but doesn't cost anything and doesn't have any ads. Also, it is just nice to see an open source game because those are so rare in the mobile world. Apple really prevented the open source community from getting big into making apps due to the apple store. It's refreshing to see a truly open source android app someone just shared because they felt like sharing just like the many open source desktop apps out there

reviews.text: In light of the fact that this game is a complete package with absolutely NO ADS, I would have happily paid more for it (and I did, as a matter of fact, purchase it on my PC after playing it on my phone). The UI and controls take a little getting used to but that is to be expected because this game made absolutely no compromises from a gameplay standpoint, and even supports keyboard and mouse on your phone, if that's your thing. This game has set the benchmark for mobile games in this genre.

reviews.text: Love this game! First off, it's not pay to win. You can pay for stuff, but it's not required at all. The gems you use to buy stuff are so easy to earn through gameplay, and you get so many gems through them. The game is so simple, yet is fun and very challenging. This game has a skill tree that upgrades your towers and other stuff like that. Overall, it's really fun, and there's nothing about the game that's really annoying.

reviews.text: Played this like 12 years ago. Still good now. Ideal sort of free game: almost as polished as a pay game - not a watered down experience. They used this game to sell several sequels, and that's where the profit came from. So if you finish this game and want more, they do have more you can buy. I wish more developers could follow this model, instead of monetizing by either cramming in tons of ads, making games pay to win, or producing a very low quality game and still cramming in constant ads.
